title: Choose Athena Studio's visual direction
question: You asked for a bolder direction. This round keeps the same image-detection workflow and operator UI task, but uses more committed visual forms. Choose one or re-roll.

options.label: Signal Field
options.thesis: A selected detection snaps into sharp focus while the rest of the signal recedes.
options.viewport: A standard project shell surrounds a high-contrast image preview, operator True/False controls, a model/source status panel, and dense sample rows; selecting a result pulls its evidence into focus and briefly inverts the preview, while all labels remain explicit.
options.risk: Pure monochrome can flatten class and review states; use text, shape, weight, and clear focus—not color alone—and disable motion under reduced-motion preferences.

options.label: Registered Sequence Folio
options.lineage: Japanese botanical folios and fixed-scale specimen plates
options.thesis: A chosen scan stays aligned across feedback and approved model versions so changes are easy to compare.
options.viewport: A standard application shell keeps the live operator preview primary; below it, four same-scale plates show the exact sample, recorded human True/False correction, reviewed candidate, and approved model version with dates and provenance.
options.case: The registered sequence makes the feedback-to-retraining lineage visible; it loses to the leader's immediate operator-state focus for everyday inference.
options.risk: The botanical reference can imply plant-domain data; use only the site's real sample and label any example as synthetic.

options.label: Claim-and-Proof Index
options.lineage: Monochrome product-marketing pages with paired evidence
options.thesis: Every status or setting is paired with the screen state that proves what it means.
options.viewport: The normal app shell presents a live preview beside each clearly labeled setting, pairing every configuration choice with its operator-facing result.
options.case: Pairing a setting with its proof helps explain the interface, but the marketing-page sequence loses the feel of a working industrial tool.
options.kept: Show the result of each consequential setting beside the control that changes it.
options.risk: Can feel like a sales page and bury the operational work.

options.label: Visible Construction Grid
options.thesis: A visible grid turns safe layout editing into a tangible, understandable act.
options.viewport: The familiar shell frames a constrained canvas of named screen regions; a clear 12-column guide, snap-to-grid layout controls, and a live scanner preview let an operator reorder approved blocks without code.
options.case: It directly supports the requested visual layout editor and makes customization legible; stronger product fit than the signal field's abstract data canvas.
options.risk: The construction grid can overpower scanner evidence; hide it in the operator preview and keep it confined to edit mode.

options.label: Durable Feedback Tickets
options.lineage: Jet-age ticket wallets, route maps, and baggage tags
options.thesis: Each human correction becomes a durable, traceable ticket toward the next approved model.
options.viewport: A standard shell keeps the inference screen central; a compact feedback ticket records the input ID, model version, operator True/False, and review status without changing the live model.
options.case: The ticket metaphor carries provenance and offline-friendly records; it does not express image detection as immediately as the leader.
options.risk: A coupon-book sequence could imply automatic progression; promotion must remain explicitly operator-approved.

options.label: Detection Atlas
options.lineage: Japanese star atlases and coordinate-field notation
options.thesis: A stable image coordinate field makes each detected region and its confidence inspectable.
options.viewport: A normal project shell surrounds one large scanner image with readable coordinate guides, detection boxes, class names, and confidence values; a selected result is ringed and its source/model IDs remain visible.
options.case: The coordinate field suits image inspection and confidence review; it is less immediately approachable than the leader for operators who just need a clear result and decision.
options.risk: A star-chart treatment may obscure the actual image; keep the source image dominant and never encode model confidence only by dot size.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The expected inspection dashboard, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: A conventional sidebar, project header, familiar data table, ordinary configuration form, and prominent live image preview with explicit operator controls.
canonCard.risk: Easy to recognize and scan, but less distinctive than the bolder forms.
